claim: Mouse Kdm1a deletion causes a dramatic reduction of PRC2 proteins.
source: Here, we show that mouse Kdm1a deletion causes a dramatic reduction of PRC2 proteins, whereas mouse null mutation of L3mbtl3 or Dcaf5 results in PRC2 accumulation and increased H3K27 trimethylation.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: Mouse null mutation of L3mbtl3 results in PRC2 accumulation and increased H3K27 trimethylation.
source: Here, we show that mouse Kdm1a deletion causes a dramatic reduction of PRC2 proteins, whereas mouse null mutation of L3mbtl3 or Dcaf5 results in PRC2 accumulation and increased H3K27 trimethylation.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: Mouse null mutation of Dcaf5 results in PRC2 accumulation and increased H3K27 trimethylation.
source: Here, we show that mouse Kdm1a deletion causes a dramatic reduction of PRC2 proteins, whereas mouse null mutation of L3mbtl3 or Dcaf5 results in PRC2 accumulation and increased H3K27 trimethylation.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: EZH2 is methylated at lysine 20 (K20).
source: The catalytic subunit of PRC2, EZH2, is methylated at lysine 20 (K20), promoting EZH2 proteolysis by L3MBTL3 and the CLR4DCAF5 ubiquitin ligase.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: K20 methylation promotes EZH2 proteolysis by L3MBTL3 and the CRL4DCAF5 ubiquitin ligase.
source: The catalytic subunit of PRC2, EZH2, is methylated at lysine 20 (K20), promoting EZH2 proteolysis by L3MBTL3 and the CLR4DCAF5 ubiquitin ligase.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: KDM1A demethylates the methylated K20 to stabilize EZH2.
source: KDM1A (LSD1) demethylates the methylated K20 to stabilize EZH2.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: K20 methylation is inhibited by AKT-mediated phosphorylation of serine 21 in EZH2.
source: K20 methylation is inhibited by AKT-mediated phosphorylation of serine 21 in EZH2.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: Mouse Ezh2K20R/K20R mutants develop hepatosplenomegaly associated with high GFI1B expression.
source: Mouse Ezh2K20R/K20R mutants develop hepatosplenomegaly associated with high GFI1B expression, and Ezh2K20R/K20R mutant bone marrows expand hematopoietic stem cells and downstream hematopoietic populations.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: Ezh2K20R/K20R mutant bone marrows expand hematopoietic stem cells and downstream hematopoietic populations.
source: Mouse Ezh2K20R/K20R mutants develop hepatosplenomegaly associated with high GFI1B expression, and Ezh2K20R/K20R mutant bone marrows expand hematopoietic stem cells and downstream hematopoietic populations.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: EZH2 is regulated by methylation-dependent proteolysis, which is negatively controlled by AKT-mediated S21 phosphorylation to establish a methylation-phosphorylation switch to regulate the PRC2 activity and hematopoiesis.
source: Our studies reveal that EZH2 is regulated by methylation-dependent proteolysis, which is negatively controlled by AKT-mediated S21 phosphorylation to establish a methylation-phosphorylation switch to regulate the PRC2 activity and hematopoiesis.
evidence: Stated in the abstract as a main finding of the study.

claim: The PRC2 epigenetically regulates embryonic development and cell fate determination.
source: The PRC2 epigenetically regulates embryonic development and cell fate determination (Chou et al., 2011; Sparmann and van Lohuizen, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The core components of PRC2 include EZH2, SUZ12, EED, and histone binding proteins RbAp48/46.
source: The core components of PRC2 include EZH2 (enhancer of Zeste homolog 2), SUZ12 (suppress of Zeste 12), EED (embryonic ectoderm development), and histone binding proteins RbAp48/46.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: EZH2 acts as the catalytic subunit of PRC2 to trimethylate histone H3 at lysine 27 (H3K27me3) to promote epigenetic gene silencing during development.
source: EZH2 acts as the catalytic subunit of PRC2 to trimethylate histone H3 at lysine 27 (H3K27me3) to promote epigenetic gene silencing during development.
evidence: Stated as established knowledge in the introduction.

claim: Mouse Ezh2, Suz12, or Eed null mutant embryos either cease to develop after implantation or initiate but fail to complete gastrulation.
source: Mouse Ezh2, Suz12, or Eed null mutant embryos either cease to develop after implantation or initiate but fail to complete gastrulation (Faust et al., 1995; O'Carroll et al., 2001; Pasini et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PRC2 represses developmental regulators in mouse embryonic stem cells.
source: PRC2 represses developmental regulators in mouse embryonic stem cells and deletion of Ezh2 compromises the self-renewal and differentiation of human embryonic stem cells by de-repressing developmental regulators (Collinson et al., 2016; Shan et al., 2017; Sparmann and van Lohuizen, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Deletion of Ezh2 compromises the self-renewal and differentiation of human embryonic stem cells by de-repressing developmental regulators.
source: PRC2 represses developmental regulators in mouse embryonic stem cells and deletion of Ezh2 compromises the self-renewal and differentiation of human embryonic stem cells by de-repressing developmental regulators (Collinson et al., 2016; Shan et al., 2017; Sparmann and van Lohuizen, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: PRC2 is required for B-lymphoid development, myogenic differentiation, and imprinted X-chromosome inactivation.
source: PRC2 is required for various other developmental functions including B-lymphoid development, myogenic differentiation, and imprinted X-chromosome inactivation, and loss of PRC2 also exhausts bone marrow hematopoietic stem cells (Chou et al., 2011; Sparmann and van Lohuizen, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Loss of PRC2 exhausts bone marrow hematopoietic stem cells.
source: PRC2 is required for various other developmental functions including B-lymphoid development, myogenic differentiation, and imprinted X-chromosome inactivation, and loss of PRC2 also exhausts bone marrow hematopoietic stem cells (Chou et al., 2011; Sparmann and van Lohuizen, 2006).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The pathological role of EZH2 is highlighted by over-expression or gain-of-function mutations in various cancers.
source: The pathological role of EZH2 is highlighted by over-expression or gain-of-function mutations in various cancers (Kim and Roberts, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: EZH2 is considered as an important marker for the aggressive stages of prostate and breast malignancies due to its high expression levels in these cancers.
source: EZH2 is considered as an important marker for the aggressive stages of prostate and breast malignancies due to its high expression levels in these cancers (Kleer et al., 2003; Varambally et al., 2002).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: EZH2 serves as a critical therapeutic target of human malignancies including hematopoietic cancers.
source: EZH2 also serves as a critical therapeutic target of human malignancies including hematopoietic cancers (Bödör et al., 2013; Chang and Hung, 2012; Kim and Roberts, 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Post-translational modifications of EZH2 play an important role in cancer development.
source: Many studies indicate that the post-translational modifications of EZH2 play an important role in cancer development (Li et al., 2020).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Serine 21 (S21) in EZH2 is phosphorylated by AKT, activated by the PI3K signaling cascade.
source: One of the critical modifications is the phosphorylation of serine 21 (S21) in EZH2 by AKT, activated by the PI3K signaling cascade (Cha et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The phosphorylated S21 was reported to inhibit EZH2 methyltransferase activity on H3K27.
source: The phosphorylated S21 was reported to inhibit EZH2 methyltransferase activity on H3K27 (Cha et al., 2005).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: AKT-mediated S21 phosphorylation on EZH2 is reported to facilitate tumorigenesis.
source: Although AKT-mediated S21 phosphorylation on EZH2 is reported to facilitate tumorigenesis (Kim et al., 2013), the physiological role and regulation of S21-phosphorylated EZH2 remain largely unclear.
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The physiological role and regulation of S21-phosphorylated EZH2 remain largely unclear.
source: Although AKT-mediated S21 phosphorylation on EZH2 is reported to facilitate tumorigenesis (Kim et al., 2013), the physiological role and regulation of S21-phosphorylated EZH2 remain largely unclear.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap in the introduction.

claim: Protein lysine methylation has been extensively investigated in histones to establish the critical roles of mono-, di-, and tri-methylated lysine residues of histones in modulating chromatin structure and gene expression.
source: Protein lysine methylation has been extensively investigated in histones to establish the critical roles of mono-, di-, and tri-methylated lysine residues of histones in modulating chromatin structure and gene expression (Greer and Shi, 2012; Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The methylations of Lys 4 (H3K4), Lys 36 (H3K36), Lys 48 (H3K48), and Lys 79 (H3K79) in histone H3 are typically associated with transcriptional gene activation.
source: For example, the methylations of Lys 4 (H3K4), Lys 36 (H3K36), Lys 48 (H3K48), and Lys 79 (H3K79) in histone H3 are typically associated with transcriptional gene activation, but the methylations of Lys 9 (H3K9) and Lys 27 (H3K27) on histone H3, or Lys 20 (H4K20) on histone H4 are usually connected to transcriptional silencing (Greer and Shi, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: The methylations of Lys 9 (H3K9) and Lys 27 (H3K27) on histone H3, or Lys 20 (H4K20) on histone H4 are usually connected to transcriptional silencing.
source: For example, the methylations of Lys 4 (H3K4), Lys 36 (H3K36), Lys 48 (H3K48), and Lys 79 (H3K79) in histone H3 are typically associated with transcriptional gene activation, but the methylations of Lys 9 (H3K9) and Lys 27 (H3K27) on histone H3, or Lys 20 (H4K20) on histone H4 are usually connected to transcriptional silencing (Greer and Shi, 2012).
evidence: Supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: Many non-histone proteins, such as p53, DNMT1, NFκB/RelA, ERα, GLI3, SOX2, LIN28A, HIF1α, and E2F1, are mono-methylated on specific lysine residues by SET7.
source: Emerging evidence indicates that many non-histone proteins, such as p53, DNA (cytosine-5)-methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), NFκB/RelA, ERα, GLI3, SOX2, LIN28A, HIF1α, and E2F1, are mono-methylated on specific lysine residues by SET7 (SET7/9, SET9, SETD7, or KMT7) (Fu et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2014b; Lee et al., 2017; Leng et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2012), originally isolated as a histone methyltransferase that mono-methylates H3K4 (Nishioka et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: SET7 was originally isolated as a histone methyltransferase that mono-methylates H3K4.
source: Emerging evidence indicates that many non-histone proteins, such as p53, DNA (cytosine-5)-methyltransferase 1 (DNMT1), NFκB/RelA, ERα, GLI3, SOX2, LIN28A, HIF1α, and E2F1, are mono-methylated on specific lysine residues by SET7 (SET7/9, SET9, SETD7, or KMT7) (Fu et al., 2016; Kim et al., 2014b; Lee et al., 2017; Leng et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2012), originally isolated as a histone methyltransferase that mono-methylates H3K4 (Nishioka et al., 2002; Wang et al., 2001).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Specific lysine-methylation on a group of non-histone proteins such as DNMT1, SOX2, SMARCC1, SMARCC2, and E2F1 by SET7 causes lysine methylation-dependent proteolysis of these non-histone proteins.
source: Our recent studies revealed that specific lysine-methylation on a group of non-histone proteins such as DNMT1, SOX2, SMARCC1, SMARCC2, and E2F1 by SET7 causes lysine methylation-dependent proteolysis of these non-histone proteins (Guo et al., 2022; Leng et al., 2018; Wang et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2019; Zhang et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature from the authors' group.

claim: The methyl groups on methylated non-histone proteins are removed by KDM1A.
source: We and others also found that the methyl groups on these methylated non-histone proteins are removed by KDM1A, initially identified as a histone demethylase that specifically removes methyl groups from the mono- and di-methylated H3K4, but not the trimethylated H3K4, to repress transcription (Guo et al., 2022; Lee et al., 2017; Leng et al., 2018; Shi et al., 2004; Wang et al., 2011; Yin et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: KDM1A was initially identified as a histone demethylase that specifically removes methyl groups from the mono- and di-methylated H3K4, but not the trimethylated H3K4, to repress transcription.
source: We and others also found that the methyl groups on these methylated non-histone proteins are removed by KDM1A, initially identified as a histone demethylase that specifically removes methyl groups from the mono- and di-methylated H3K4, but not the trimethylated H3K4, to repress transcription (Guo et al., 2022; Lee et al., 2017; Leng et al., 2018; Shi et al., 2004; Wang et al., 2011; Yin et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2013; Zhang et al., 2012).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The mouse null mutation of Kdm1a causes early embryonic lethality.
source: The mouse null mutation of Kdm1a causes early embryonic lethality (Wang et al., 2009; Wang et al., 2007).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Loss of mouse Kdm1a profoundly impairs the self-renewal and differentiation of various stem/progenitor cells such as embryonic stem cells and hematopoietic stem cells.
source: Loss of mouse Kdm1a also profoundly impairs the self-renewal and differentiation of various stem/progenitor cells such as embryonic stem cells and hematopoietic stem cells (Adamo et al., 2011; Saleque et al., 2007; Zhang et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: The molecular targets of Kdm1a deficiency that cause pathological defects remain largely unclear.
source: However, the molecular targets of Kdm1a deficiency that cause these pathological defects remain largely unclear.
evidence: Stated as a knowledge gap in the introduction.

claim: Homozygous loss of Kdm1a conditional alleles by breeding with the Nestin-Cre mice caused animal lethality immediately after birth on day one (P0).
source: Homozygous loss of Kdm1a conditional alleles by breeding with the Nestin-Cre mice caused animal lethality immediately after birth on day one (P0, Figure 1A).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The protein level of EZH2 is significantly reduced in the Kdm1a null mutant mice.
source: Immunostaining of brain sections from the wild-type and Kdm1a null mutant animals revealed that the protein level of EZH2 is significantly reduced in the Kdm1a null mutant mice (Figure 1A).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The protein levels of key components of PRC2, including EZH2, SUZ12, and EED, are markedly reduced in the brain extracts of Kdm1a null mutants, as compared with those of wild-type littermates.
source: Further characterization repeatedly showed that the protein levels of key components of PRC2, including EZH2, SUZ12, and EED, are markedly reduced in the brain extracts of Kdm1a null mutants, as compared with those of wild-type littermates (Figure 1B).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The Kdm1a deletion-induced reduction of PRC2 protein levels occurred post-transcriptionally.
source: The Kdm1a deletion-induced reduction of these PRC2 protein levels occurred post-transcriptionally, since the mRNA levels of the PRC2 key components are comparable between the Kdm1a null mutants and the wild-type littermates in the brain tissues (Figure 1C).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Induced deletion of Kdm1a in the CAGGCre-ER/Kdm1afl/fl MEFs by addition of 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OH-Tam) led to the rapid disappearance of PRC2 proteins and reduction of H3K27me3.
source: While the wild-type MEFs normally express substantial levels of PRC2 proteins, induced deletion of Kdm1a in the CAGGCre-ER/Kdm1afl/fl MEFs by addition of 4-hydroxytamoxifen (4-OH-Tam) led to the rapid disappearance of these PRC2 proteins and reduction of H3K27me3 (Figure 1D).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The protein level of EZH2 is significantly decreased by CBB3001, a KDM1A inhibitor.
source: We treated the CAGGCre-ER/Kdm1afl/fl MEFs with a KDM1A inhibitor, CBB3001, that we previously developed (Guo et al., 2022; Hoang et al., 2018) and found that the protein level of EZH2 is significantly decreased by CBB3001 (Figure 1E).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Kdm1a silencing caused the downregulation of EZH2 protein and the Kdm1a silencing-induced EZH2 reduction is reversed by the treatment of 26 S proteasome inhibitor, MG132.
source: We found that Kdm1a silencing caused the downregulation of EZH2 protein and the Kdm1a silencing-induced EZH2 reduction is reversed by the treatment of 26 S proteasome inhibitor, MG132, added in the last 6 hr of the experiment (Figure 1G; Guo et al., 2022).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1G.

claim: Expression of the wild-type, but not the catalytically dead mutant, can suppress the si-Kdm1a-3'UTR effects of the endogenous Kdm1a on EZH2 proteins.
source: We found that while the siRNA against the 3'UTR region (si-Kdm1a-3'UTR) of the endogenous Kdm1a leads to the downregulation of EZH2 in the absence of the Flag-KDM1A, expression of the wild-type, but not the catalytically dead mutant, can suppress the si-Kdm1a-3'UTR effects of the endogenous Kdm1a on EZH2 proteins (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: KDM1A is required to maintain the protein stability of EZH2 to prevent the disassembly of PRC2.
source: Our studies indicate that KDM1A is required to maintain the protein stability of EZH2 to prevent the disassembly of PRC2.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claim: The levels of EZH2 and SUZ12 proteins are significantly increased in the mouse L3mbtl3 null embryos, as compared to that of the wild-type littermates.
source: We repeatedly found that the levels of EZH2 and SUZ12 proteins are significantly increased in the mouse L3mbtl3 null embryos, which died at E17.5–19.5, as compared to that of the wild-type littermates (Figure 2A).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The loss of L3mbtl3 caused the accumulation of EZH2 protein and the increased level of trimethylated H3K27 in mouse embryonic fibroblasts.
source: In mouse embryonic fibroblasts isolated from the wild-type or L3mbtl3 homozygous deletion mutant embryos, the loss of L3mbtl3 caused the accumulation of EZH2 protein and the increased level of trimethylated H3K27 (Figure 2B).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Homozygous loss of L3mbtl3 in the brain of the L3mbtl3fl/fl/Nestin-Cre mice accumulated EZH2 and SUZ12 proteins, as compared with that of L3mbtl3fl/+/Nestin-Cre mice.
source: We found that homozygous loss of L3mbtl3 in the brain of the L3mbtl3fl/fl/Nestin-Cre mice survived, but the brain extracts accumulated EZH2 and SUZ12 proteins, as compared with that of L3mbtl3fl/+/Nestin-Cre mice (Figure 2C).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: The protein levels of EZH2 and trimethylated H3K27 accumulate in the L3mbtl3 conditional null mutant brains, as compared to that of the control wild-type littermates.
source: Our immunostaining of the brain sections from the wild-type and L3mbtl3fl/fl/Nestin-Cre null mutant animals also revealed that the protein levels of EZH2 and trimethylated H3K27 accumulate in the L3mbtl3 conditional null mutant brains, as compared to that of the control wild-type littermates (Figure 2D).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: The induced co-deletion of Kdm1a and L3mbtl3 in the CAGGCre-ER/ Kdm1afl/fl/L3mbtl3fl/fl MEFs leads to the restoration of the EZH2 and H3K27me3 protein levels in the MEFs.
source: However, the induced co-deletion of Kdm1a and L3mbtl3 in the CAGGCre-ER/ Kdm1afl/fl/L3mbtl3fl/fl MEFs leads to the restoration of the EZH2 and H3K27me3 protein levels in the MEFs.
evidence: Stated in the results section.

claim: While Kdm1a silencing reduced EZH2 protein levels, co-silencing of L3mbtl3 and Kdm1a stabilized EZH2 protein levels in Kdm1a-deficient cells.
source: Our study revealed that while Kdm1a silencing reduced EZH2 protein levels, co-silencing of L3mbtl3 and Kdm1a stabilized EZH2 protein levels in Kdm1a-deficient cells (Figure 2F and G).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2F and G.

claim: EZH2 protein levels are elevated in the CRISPR-Cas9-mediated L3mbtl3 knockout (KO) cells than the parental wild-type HCT116 cells.
source: Analysis of EZH2 protein revealed that EZH2 protein levels are elevated in the CRISPR-Cas9-mediated L3mbtl3 knockout (KO) cells than the parental wild-type HCT116 cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: L3MBTL3 overexpression in HCT116 cells caused the downregulation of EZH2 protein.
source: Our studies showed that L3MBTL3 overexpression in HCT116 cells caused the downregulation of EZH2 protein (Figure 2—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2B.

claim: The protein level of EZH2 is tightly regulated by L3MBTL3.
source: Collectively, these studies indicate the protein level of EZH2 is tightly regulated by L3MBTL3.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claim: L3MBTL3 recruits the CRL4DCAF5 ubiquitin E3 ligase complex to target substrates, such as DNMT1, SOX2, and SMARCC1, for ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis.
source: Our previous studies have shown that L3MBTL3 recruits the CRL4DCAF5 ubiquitin E3 ligase complex to target substrates, such as DNMT1, SOX2, and SMARCC1, for ubiquitin-dependent proteolysis (Guo et al., 2022; Leng et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: Supported by citations to previous literature from the authors' group.

claim: Homozygous mutation of the Dcaf5 alleles caused significant elevation of EZH2 and H3K27me3 protein levels.
source: We found that homozygous mutation of the Dcaf5 alleles also caused significant elevation of EZH2 and H3K27me3 protein levels (Figure 3C).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Loss of Dcaf5 leads to increased levels of EZH2 and H3K27me3 staining, as compared with that of control wild-type littermates.
source: Immunostaining of the embryonic brain sections revealed that loss of Dcaf5 leads to increased levels of EZH2 and H3K27me3 staining, as compared with that of control wild-type littermates (Figure 3D).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3D.

claim: siRNA-mediated co-silencing of Dcaf5 and Kdm1a in H1299 cells stabilized EZH2 protein in Kdm1a-deficient cells.
source: Consistent with these animal studies, siRNA-mediated co-silencing of Dcaf5 and Kdm1a in H1299 cells with two representative siRNAs stabilized EZH2 protein in Kdm1a-deficient cells (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3E and F.

claim: The CRL4DCAF5 ubiquitin ligase complex is involved in the proteolytic degradation of EZH2 to regulate the H3K27me3 levels during mouse development and in cultured cancer cells.
source: These results indicate that the CRL4DCAF5 ubiquitin ligase complex is involved in the proteolytic degradation of EZH2 to regulate the H3K27me3 levels during mouse development and in cultured cancer cells.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claim: EZH2 contains a conserved lysine residue, Lys20 (K20), in the putative SET7 methylation consensus motif (R/K-S/T/V-K) that is very similar to that of the Lys42 (K42) methylation degron motif in SOX2.
source: To further investigate EZH2 regulation, we examined and found that EZH2 contains a conserved lysine residue, Lys20 (K20), in the putative SET7 methylation consensus motif (R/K-S/T/V-K) that is very similar to that of the Lys42 (K42) methylation degron motif in SOX2 (Figure 4A; Zhang et al., 2018; Zhang et al., 2019).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The recombinant GST-KDM1A protein can effectively remove the methyl group of the monomethylated K20 peptide.
source: We mixed and incubated the monomethylated K20 peptide with purified GST-KDM1A and found that the recombinant GST-KDM1A protein can effectively remove the methyl group of the monomethylated K20 peptide (Figure 4C), indicating that the monomethylated K20 in EZH2 serves as a direct substrate of KDM1A.
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4C.

claim: The monomethylated K20 in EZH2 serves as a direct substrate of KDM1A.
source: We mixed and incubated the monomethylated K20 peptide with purified GST-KDM1A and found that the recombinant GST-KDM1A protein can effectively remove the methyl group of the monomethylated K20 peptide (Figure 4C), indicating that the monomethylated K20 in EZH2 serves as a direct substrate of KDM1A.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section based on experimental data.

claim: Loss of KDM1A destabilizes both EZH2 and EZH2-K20me and reduces the level of H3K27me3 in HCT116 cells, but treatment of KDM1A-deficient cells with the protease inhibitor MG132 restored the levels of EZH2, EZH2-K20me, and H3K27me3.
source: Loss of KDM1A destabilizes both EZH2 and EZH2-K20me and reduces the level of H3K27me3 in HCT116 cells, but treatment of KDM1A-deficient cells with the protease inhibitor MG132 restored the levels of EZH2, EZH2-K20me, and H3K27me3 (Figure 4D).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Nestin-Cre-mediated loss of Kdm1a in the mouse caused the reduction of both the K20 methylation level of EZH2 and the EZH2 protein levels, as well as the downregulation of trimethylated H3K27 levels.
source: As shown in Figure 4E, Nestin-Cre-mediated loss of Kdm1a in the mouse caused the reduction of both the K20 methylation level of EZH2 and the EZH2 protein levels, as well as the downregulation of trimethylated H3K27 levels.
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Homozygous loss of L3mbtl3 resulted in an increased level of EZH2 K20me.
source: Conversely, homozygous loss of L3mbtl3 resulted in an increased level of EZH2 K20me (Figure 4F).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4F.

claim: Transient overexpression of SET7 resulted in a reduction of EZH2 protein and H3K27 trimethylation levels in HCT116 cells.
source: We found that transient overexpression of SET7 resulted in a reduction of EZH2 protein and H3K27 trimethylation levels in HCT116 cells (Figure 4G).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4G.

claim: The K20-methylated EZH2 fraction is enriched in the L3MBTL3 co-immunoprecipitation with EZH2 in SET7-expressed and MG132-treated cells.
source: In addition, the K20-methylated EZH2 fraction is enriched in the L3MBTL3 co-immunoprecipitation with EZH2 in SET7-expressed and MG132-treated cells (Figure 4H).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4H.

claim: While silencing of Kdm1a reduced the protein level of ectopically and stably expressed Flag-tagged EZH2 in H1299 cells, co-silencing of Set7 with Kdm1a siRNAs effectively re-stabilized Flag-EZH2 protein in KDM1A-deficient cells.
source: Our investigation further showed that while silencing of Kdm1a reduced the protein level of ectopically and stably expressed Flag-tagged EZH2 in H1299 cells, co-silencing of Set7 with Kdm1a siRNAs effectively re-stabilized Flag-EZH2 protein in KDM1A-deficient cells (Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4I and Figure 4—figure supplement 2A.

claim: SET7 is capable of methylating K20 in EZH2, and that the methylated K20 of EZH2 is targeted by L3MBTL3 for methylation-dependent proteolysis of EZH2.
source: These studies indicate that SET7 is capable of methylating K20 in EZH2, and that the methylated K20 of EZH2 is targeted by L3MBTL3 for methylation-dependent proteolysis of EZH2.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion in the results section.

claim: Silencing of Phf20l1 by two independent siRNAs both induced the degradation of EZH2 protein, and co-silencing of Phf20l1 and L3mbtl3 restored EZH2 protein levels.
source: We found that silencing of Phf20l1 by two independent siRNAs both induced the degradation of EZH2 protein, and co-silencing of Phf20l1 and L3mbtl3 restored EZH2 protein levels (Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and C).
evidence: Stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2B and C.

claim: PHF20L1 normally prevents the proteolysis of EZH2 by the methylation-dependent proteolysis.
